packageRules.description: GitHub Actions and pre-commit hooks never reach the published tarball (`files` is css/*, scss/*, scripts/*), so updating one must never bump the package version. Pinning the scope to `actions` makes the shared releaseRule `{type: chore, scope: actions, release: false}` match every time, for patch, minor and major alike -- verified that the rule also suppresses `chore(actions)!` and a BREAKING CHANGE footer. Renovate was otherwise emitting `chore(deps)` for some of these updates, which releases a patch, or `chore(deps)!` for majors, which releases a minor. To release deliberately, retitle the PR: squash is this repo's only merge method and squash_merge_commit_title is COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE, so the title you set is the commit subject semantic-release reads.

devDependencies never reach consumers, so updating one must never release. The literal prefix is needed because the shared preset's major rule sets commitMessagePrefix 'chore(deps)!: ', which a packageRule can only override, not unset; 'chore(actions)' maps to release: false in @ivuorinen/semantic-release-config. The separate group keeps dev updates out of groups that also hold runtime dependencies (the preset's stylelint group holds the runtime stylelint-config-* packages and the dev stylelint here), whose PR title would otherwise decide the release for both.
pre-commit hook majors: the shared preset restores the 'chore(actions): ' prefix for github-actions majors only, so without this a hook major still arrives as 'chore(deps)!: ' and releases a major.
